title: Software Foundation · know which file to edit

scenes.title: Find the small part that does your work
sentences: A modern codebase contains algorithms, graphical interfaces, device access, build rules, and delivery tools. That volume can make even a simple change hard to locate.
Software Foundation gives those recurring responsibilities a reusable structure. Use the optional editor or work directly in the source.
We will follow a small processing application from its button to its algorithm and back to a result, with the exact files visible at every step.
lines: Task → exact file → small function → result

scenes.title: Create your project; keep a known baseline
sentences: From a foundation checkout, run fork dot sh with your project name and a fresh destination.
The helper creates an independent repository from the latest main baseline, without a configured remote.
Read the agent instructions, then ask your coding assistant to work within the existing build, interface, and test structure.
If you want visual editing, ask it to follow the editor’s project schema, typed event bindings, and block interfaces documented in the editor readme.
The walkthrough uses copies of the small editor examples so the reference remains intact.

scenes.title: Four files answer four everyday questions
sentences: Begin in editor, examples, simple C. This is a small application with its own source files.
To change the calculation, open signal dot C. To change what a button does, open events dot C.
To arrange controls and connect blocks, edit project dot JSON through the visual editor.
To add compiled files, edit CMakeLists. You can work on these specific responsibilities while the platform adapters and retained dependency machinery support them underneath.

scenes.title: Here is the entire gain calculation
sentences: This is the actual calculation in signal dot C, at lines twenty through twenty two.
One sample and a gain go in. Their product comes out.
With the four source samples one, two, three, and four, a gain of two produces two, four, six, and eight.
The function contains no window toolkit, workflow service, or editor interface. Its declaration is in signal dot H, and a flow adapter supplies samples to it.

scenes.title: Change one expression; check the result
sentences: For a concrete edit, add one to each amplified sample. Change the return expression in your copy of signal dot C.
The inputs and gain stay the same. The outputs should now be three, five, seven, and nine.
The accompanying replay script compiles both versions and checks those exact values.
When changing the full starter application, update its expected results in main dot C P P as well. A failed old expectation is useful feedback that behavior changed.

scenes.title: Use Files and Find to go straight to the function
sentences: You can navigate these files inside the editor. Choose Files, enter the project-relative path, and open it.
Find the function by name instead of scanning an entire file.
Here we open events dot C, find the run handler, then open signal dot C and find the gain function. CMakeLists is available in the same file view.
Double-clicking a bound widget or processing block provides another direct route to its source.

scenes.title: The event chooses when the calculation runs
sentences: Events dot C describes the button action. This excerpt sets the processing message, runs the samples, and displays the result.
The surrounding handler reads the gain choice and manages the enabled state of the Run button.
Change this file when the sequence of user actions should change. Change signal dot C when the mathematics should change.
The small C plus plus adapter translates the C callbacks to the shared user interface.

scenes.title: Place a widget; retain the layout
sentences: In Forms, choose a widget kind and Add widget. Set its label and position, then Apply.
This new button is named Reset output.
The design lives in project dot JSON. Save also writes generated form and event headers.
Preview shows the layout without running application handlers. A running application combines that layout with the ordinary source files we just located.

scenes.title: Give the new button an ordinary handler
sentences: Choose Activate or click, then Edit code on Reset output. A new binding creates a typed C plus plus handler skeleton.
Its source path is shown at the top of the code window.
Include signal dot H, call the ordinary C state initialization function, then set the output text through the UI object.
Save the source, close the window, and save the design. The accompanying check dispatches this exact generated binding and verifies its result.

scenes.title: C++ keeps the same small-function pattern
sentences: The Simple C plus plus example uses the same organization.
Its signal dot C P P owns this gain calculation. Events dot C P P owns the button behavior, and services dot H P P holds application state.
You can write a short procedural function like this, or use classes, templates, and existing libraries.
The visual layer connects to ordinary source. It does not replace the language or require your algorithm to be written as GUI code.

scenes.title: Know which layer owns the change
sentences: Think of three layers. Your functions own the behavior. The saved design and generated headers connect the interface and graph. Adapters and toolchains make that application work on its hosts.
Editing an algorithm usually means changing its source and tests. Adding a platform capability can require the shared contract and adapters.
Generated files are useful to inspect, but make layout changes in the design so the next generation preserves your intent.

scenes.title: Add a source file to the correct target
sentences: For another C algorithm, create a source file and its declaration header. Then add the source to the target that compiles your C behavior.
In Simple C, that target is simple C behavior. C plus plus adapters belong to the application executable target.
Include the new header in its caller and call the helper. The source list tells the compiler what to build.
Opening a file in the visual editor alone does not enroll it in compilation. Reconfigure and rebuild after changing the target inputs.

scenes.title: Rust has the same clear working set
sentences: The tutorial includes a separate, small mixed-language example that you can build and run.
Rust gain dot R S and smoother dot R S hold the processing functions. Lib dot R S declares those modules and exports a small C interface.
The matching declarations live in F F I dot H. The C plus plus application calls them from an event-style function.
This makes the algorithm, language boundary, and caller easy to find independently.

scenes.title: Call C and Rust from C++ behavior
sentences: This is the actual caller in the accompanying example. A C helper clips the input. A Rust function applies the gain. Another Rust function smooths the value while C plus plus retains the previous result.
A GUI handler can call the same functions and then update its widget.
Our console check calls this event-style function twice and verifies results of two and three. The complete build and checks are retained with the video sources.

scenes.title: Add a Rust module and its build dependency
sentences: Here, smoother dot R S is the added Rust file. Declare its module in lib dot R S, and export the function through the C interface.
Include its matching declaration from F F I dot H in the caller. The CMake rule compiles a static archive and links it into the application.
List the new module in that rule’s dependencies so edits trigger a rebuild. Run these commands from the language integration example directory.
Keep types and ownership explicit at the language boundary. For Foundation applications on other targets, follow the documented target-matched SDK route.
code: # CMakeLists.txt: keep every module in DEPENDS

scenes.title: Follow a processing block into Rust
sentences: The Rust DSP project provides a larger algorithm example. Double-click the processing block to open D S P dot R S, and locate process samples.
That function owns the filter mathematics and state across chunks. It applies a three-tap filter and decimates by two.
D S P dot H declares the interface. Flow adapter dot C P P translates stream buffers into calls.
Change the algorithm in the Rust file, and change the graph composition in the visual flow.

scenes.title: Wire several inputs and outputs
sentences: Advanced MIMO demonstrates two inputs and four independently accounted outputs.
The Ports and source panel identifies the block factory, source file, and typed ports. The graph connects an output to an input of the same type.
Each port can consume or produce a different number of values. Bounded queues provide backpressure.
You can use this structure for signal processing, computer vision, and other continuing data work, with your own algorithms behind the blocks.

scenes.title: Find the equivalent files in the main application
sentences: The starter examples are teaching projects. The repository’s main Entry list application has its own corresponding files.
The record behavior is in source, store dot C P P, with its public interface under include.
Shared application actions live in the GUI shared application file. Its widget definition lives beside it.
The default Rust validator is under Rust, text validation, source, lib dot R S. Use the architecture document to locate the equivalent responsibility as your application grows.

scenes.title: Explore the change, then the exact source
sentences: Open documentation tool, published, index dot HTML in a local browser. The included explorer needs no web server, AI service, or documentation rebuild.
Choose Add a widget and click handler, then Declare the widget. The panel explains what to change, why, the exact file, and a source example.
Parameter guides help decode dense declarations. Add a source file to the compiler leads to the target that owns your code.
This snapshot maps the main application we just located. Its capture date is shown; compare it with current source when making changes.

scenes.title: Use the matching PDF collection
sentences: The explorer also links to corresponding PDFs. Edit paths contains the widget and source-file recipes. Compiler reference contains the target declarations.
The remaining volumes cover code walkthroughs, execution flows, code flowcharts, and a separately labeled AI-authored GUI mental model.
Keep the published folder together so local links can work. PDF navigation depends on the viewer.
For current instructions, use docs slash readme as the topic index and the editor readme for its separate visual-project workflow.
callouts: HTML + six PDF volumes, available locally

scenes.title: Build with known tools and retained inputs
sentences: The default application combines C plus plus with Rust. Follow the listed host prerequisites, then use build dot sh and the focused core check.
For controlled or offline work, restore the verified, target-matched SDK inputs before building.
These retain toolchains, dependencies, source, and integrity records, reducing reliance on future upstream availability.
The application shares behavior across seven GUI hosts. The optional editor has its own FLTK, Rev, and SDL framebuffer hosts and qualification record.

scenes.title: Your CI-built Latest release is the package repository
sentences: Software Foundation connects systems that are usually maintained separately.
GitHub Actions builds and checks the application, creates native packages, and formats signed repository indexes as release assets.
A P T and pacman point directly to the project’s GitHub Latest download root. Normal operating-system package updates discover the promoted release and fetch its packages there.
Gentoo follows Latest through the verified Portage adapter. This delivery route needs no independent package-repository server. The installed and distribution guides provide the exact client setup.

scenes.title: Make the next change easy to find
sentences: The daily loop is concrete. Name the behavior, open its owning file, change the small function or visual composition, and check the result.
Save or generate after layout and wiring changes. Rebuild after source changes. Keep expected values and failure cases explicit.
The optional editor, local documentation, and prepared toolchains also support continued development when frontier AI providers are down.
Future projects repeatedly need these capabilities. People and AI agents can begin with the connections established and concentrate on their project’s important work.
